about: Six hats. One agent can wear them in turn (`audit.py next` says which), or each hat can be given to its own agent (`audit.py hat SESSION ID` prints that hat's whole brief). A hat may run only the skills listed here, and the command refuses anything else. Every hat writes into the same session folder, so the chief of staff can put the findings together.
never_for_every_hat: write to, change or delete anything in the person's app, the system behind it or any file of theirs: the audit sends no write that it can see (it refuses HTTP requests that are not reads, gives a WebSocket nowhere to go, and lists what it refused); it cannot know whether a GET has an effect on the server
put the person's data into this repository or into any file outside the session folder
say a check passed when it was not run, or that it covers more than its 'cannot find' list says
decide for the person: where the answer is a choice, say what the choice is and ask

hats.name: Database and data analyst
hats.purpose: Find out whether what is on the screen really comes from the data, and what the screen does when the data is empty, wrong or missing.
asks_the_person: Which screen shows the data you know best, and what do you do to get to it?
Is any of what the screen shows meant to be worked out (a count, a total, a percentage)? From what?
looks_for: values typed in
values that stay when their source changes
values shown after the source failed
counts that are not the number of records

hands_to.ui-ux: what the screen shows when there is no data, so they can judge whether a person would notice
hands_to.systems-requirements: which fields and records to check against the person's own data

hats.name: UI/UX engineer
hats.purpose: Decide whether a person looking at the screen could tell live data from cached, sample, empty and failed. The worry is a screen that looks right and is not.
asks_the_person: When something is wrong with the data, how would you want the screen to tell you?
Can you tell, looking at this screen, whether the data is from now?
looks_for: no sign of where the data came from or when
an error that looks like normal
an empty screen that looks like loading
colour as the only cue

hands_to.data-analyst: a state that looks wrong but may be right, to confirm from the data
hands_to.chief-of-staff: what to change in the screen, in plain words, and the pictures

hats.name: Systems requirements engineer
hats.purpose: Check that the records a person knows are on the screen with the right ID, the right text and the right fields, word for word.
asks_the_person: Which five requirements do you know by heart, or can check against the source in a minute?
Which fields must never be wrong or missing (ID, text, owner, level, status, links)?
looks_for: a requirement shown with another one's text
an ID that was invented or reformatted
text that was changed, cut or reflowed
a field shown under the wrong heading

hands_to.data-analyst: a field mapping that looks wrong, to trace
hands_to.configuration-management: a record that changed between two copies
hands_to.chief-of-staff: the sheet the person ticked, and what it showed

hats.name: Configuration management
hats.purpose: Say what changed between two copies of the data, whether anything outside what was meant to change did, and where a second copy of the data is kept (in the source, or in the browser). Nothing is written back: a person reads the difference first.
asks_the_person: Which two copies of the data (before and after) should be compared, and which fields were meant to change?
Who has to approve a change before it goes back to the source, and where is that approval written? (No check reads an approval or a baseline off the screen: write what they say in the minutes.)
looks_for: changes nobody asked for
records added or removed
a second source of truth kept in the browser
sample data in files the page loads

hands_to.data-analyst: a value that looks older than the rest, to trace
hands_to.scribe: the approval, in the person's words
hands_to.chief-of-staff: the diff, and whether it is inside what was meant to change

hats.name: Scribe
hats.purpose: Keep the record: what was run, what was found, what the person said and decided. Nothing else.
asks_the_person: Is that what you decided? (read it back in their words before writing it)
looks_for: a decision with no name and no time
a finding with no entry saying what was done about it

hands_to.chief-of-staff: the minutes, so open items can be listed

hats.name: Chief of staff
hats.purpose: Put the other hats' findings together, say what matters first, what has not been looked at and why, and what the person has to decide.
asks_the_person: Which of these should be fixed before anyone uses the screen on real work?
Is it all right not to run the checks listed as not run?
looks_for: a hat that has not been worn
a check nobody ran and nobody skipped
the same finding reported by two hats
